notes:
CR: enterprise evaluation focused on Reserved GPU pools across NA / EU / APAC. Key asks: throughput guarantees, latency SLOs, and explicit failover headroom per region.

Highlights / customer voice: 
- Primary workloads: low-latency customer-facing chat (support agent & personalization) + embeddings-heavy search for real-time ranking. Quote from CTO: "latency variance kills user trust — need predictable p95/p99, not just averages."
- Targets discussed: p95 latency target ~150ms for short-turn chat flows (summary + intent), p99 target <= 350ms under steady-state; throughput baseline ~1k concurrent in NA, 600 EU, 200 APAC with burst tolerance to 3k total.
- Reserved planning ask: propose reserved pool sizes per region with explicit failover headroom. They expect: steady reserve = observed baseline * 1.25, recommended commit = steady reserve * 1.3-1.5 depending on risk appetite. They want a 30% cross-region failover headroom assumption for worst-case AZ/regional outage.
- Architecture preference: active-active between NA and EU for latency-sensitive routes; APAC can be active-passive until traffic grows. Want clear routing policy for model fallback: prefer quantized-compatible model variant when primary capacity saturates (automatic fallback).
- SLA negotiation points: 99.95% region-level uptime, credits scaled by minutes downtime, MTTR target < 2 hours for priority incidents, and a runbook handover during rollouts. They explicitly asked for per-route SLOs (chat vs embeddings) and token-level cost transparency for budgeting.
- Cost tradeoffs: committed GPU-hours vs on-demand bursting. They want a pro forma showing incremental unit cost for reserved vs on-demand and a 'break-even' compute-hours estimate.
- Security / compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration for customer keys, audit logs shipped to their SIEM, and optional data residency controls per-region.

Open items / asks for Redwood:
- Provide regional sizing spreadsheet (per-AZ GPU counts, baseline vs reserved, recommended reserve multiplier).
- Clarify multi-region failover mechanism: automated cross-region capacity siphon vs DNS-level failover; details on expected RTO and dependencies (VPC peering, egress).
- Explicit SLA language sample (financial credits + MTTR) for procurement team.
- Example workload trace (token-level RPS) template they can fill to finalize sizing.
